description: Indian-origin NASA astronaut Anil Menon just accomplished his inaugural spacewalk outside the International Space Station alongside astronaut Jessica Meir. This essential task involved enhancing the power system of the ISS, ensuring its energy supply remains sustainable for many future missions. Menon's milestone underscores India’s expanding role in global space exploration and innovation.

title: AIFF considers withdrawing from FIFA ASEAN Cup in favour of India vs Brazil game

While most Executive Committee members favour the marquee clash, former India captain Bhaichung Bhutia has urged the federation to back the tournament for its sporting and financial benefits.

title: 'Auqib Nabi shouldn't have come as a replacement': Ex-cricketer on India squad
description: Auqib Nabi earned a place in India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka series. He replaces the injured fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah in the team. Nabi's selection follows his strong performances in domestic cricket competitions. He took 104 wickets across two exceptional Ranji Trophy seasons. Nabi becomes the first cricketer from Jammu and Kashmir to reach this milestone.

title: 'We are not enemies': Rijiju meets Rahul again to break Parliament logjam
Australia removed island rabbits in 1986; native habitat is returning
description: Phillip Island has undergone a remarkable environmental turnaround following an extensive pest eradication initiative. The island is witnessing a resurgence of native flora and is nurturing thriving colonies of migratory seabirds. Each year, it becomes a safe haven for thousands of seabirds to breed. Ongoing restoration efforts aim to safeguard native wildlife and reinforce vulnerable soil ecosystems, making it a crucial sanctuary for reptiles that have vanished from other regions.

title: Meta admits to 'serious issues' in talks with govt over CSAM, deepfakes & bots
description: Meta's international team is in ongoing talks with Indian government representatives today, aiming to align with local laws and tackle content moderation challenges. Officials are requesting insights into algorithms and preventive measures against harmful content. They are also discussing WhatsApp policies and strategies to combat CSAM. A meeting between IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Meta's global team is expected later today.

title: On the frontlines: How Indian sailors are paying the price in Middle East war
description: India's maritime workers are confronting unprecedented challenges as wartime conflicts reconfigure shipping routes into perilous zones. The recent loss of life among Indian sailors in attacks on commercial vessels has raised alarm. With many enduring extended time away from home and facing harsh conditions at sea, their families live in constant worry about their safety. The call for better protection and governmental assistance for these seafarers is intensifying.

title: India gets its first woman 'Top Gun': Bhawana Kanth scripts IAF history
description: Squadron Leader Bhawana Kanth achieved a historic milestone by clearing the Fighter Combat Leader course. This demanding program trains officers in advanced combat tactics and spans twenty weeks. She is the first woman pilot from the Indian Air Force to achieve this distinction. The Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment is a premier institution for operational edge. This achievement highlights continued progress for women in the Indian Air Force.

title: Chicago tree cover linked to fewer deaths; 14,000 trees cut 105 deaths
description: A new study by Northwestern University has found that neighbourhoods in Chicago that lost more tree canopy over 11 years also recorded higher mortality rates, particularly in hotter areas. The researchers say protecting mature trees, along with planting new ones, could help reduce heat-related health risks and improve public health in cities.

title: Kentucky family rejects $26M offer for farm land over ‘poison’ data center
description: A Kentucky family has refused a substantial $26 million offer for their farmland.  The anonymous company wanted to build a large AI data center on their property.  The family prioritizes protecting farmland and food resources over financial gain.  Generations have farmed this land, contributing to national food supplies.  Other landowners nearby have reportedly agreed to sell their properties.

Who is Lucky Rawat? India's only student selected for North Pole mission

After clearing a rigorous international selection process, he is joining students from 22 countries on a scientific voyage to the North Pole, highlighting how talent and perseverance can open extraordinary global opportunities.

title: 'No one was allowed': Rahane reveals MS Dhoni's one strict rule

Dhoni's own playing future remains uncertain following an injury and missed IPL season.

title: 'Save me': Eyewitness recounts Atiq Ahmed son's final moments after fatal crash
description: Abaan Ahmed, the youngest of Atiq Ahmed's children, tragically passed away in a road accident in Jhansi. His SUV hit a divider, resulting in his immediate death and that of a friend. Three other friends sustained injuries and are under medical care. Investigators are looking into differing accounts surrounding the crash. The burial of Abaan Ahmed is planned for Friday in Prayagraj.

title: Most expensive surface warship programme? US Navy's Trump-class battleship could cost $275 billion
description: A new Congressional Budget Office report details the US Navy's proposed Trump-class battleship program. This ambitious fleet of fifteen vessels is projected to cost an estimated $275 billion over nearly three decades. The program's high expense stems from the ships' unprecedented size and advanced nuclear propulsion systems. Meeting the planned schedule would require doubling large surface combatant production by 2035.

title: Taxation bill clears Lok Sabha, allows provision for MDR on UPI transactions
description: Under the proposed changes, the Central government would be empowered to specify, through a notification, the electronic payment modes or transactions that must continue to remain free of charges.

title: 'Kya Bolti Public': CJP announces nationwide 'pressure campaign' from September
description: The Cockroach Janata Party is stepping in as a public pressure group, primarily targeting pressing issues such as unemployment and education reform across the country. Set to launch their 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign in September, they aim to engage the youth in dialogue for transparency and accountability. Moreover, the CJP is determined to tackle escalating education costs and improve the reliability of media.

title: From Bhargavastra to Indrajaal: How India's drone killers take on hostile UAVs, swarms
description: India is rapidly developing advanced counter-drone systems to counter aerial threats.  Indigenous systems like Bhargavastra and Indrajaal offer diverse engagement capabilities.  BEL's D4 system integrates multiple neutralization methods onto a single platform.  The DRDO's precision-guided munitions extend aerial threat engagement options.  These developments position India to effectively manage evolving drone warfare challenges.

title: England recall Cook, Ollie Pope for Pakistan Tests; Joe Root to lead

title: 'Soren unfit to hold office': Protesting students demand Jharkhand CM resign

We now demand the chief minister's resignation, as he is unfit for the office he holds. It has been so long since he returned from Bengaluru, yet he has taken no cognisance of the situation."

title: Scientists reveal how green roofs cut rooftop temperatures by 40°F
description: Green roofs offer a solution to urban heat by absorbing sunlight and releasing water. Vegetation shades surfaces and evapotranspiration naturally cools surrounding areas. These living roofs also manage rainwater and provide habitats for urban wildlife. Extensive and intensive systems cater to different building needs and budgets. Cities worldwide are adopting green roofs to combat rising temperatures and improve environments.

title: 'Convey sentiments to Amit Shah': RS Chair to Rijiju after oppn seeks his presence
description: Parliament proceedings faced disruptions as opposition parties demanded Union home minister Amit Shah's statement. Rajya Sabha Chairman asked Kiren Rijiju to convey the opposition's sentiments to the home minister. Mallikarjun Kharge reiterated the demand for a statement and discussion on the police action. Rijiju said Kharge had not cited any rule while making the request.

title: 'Political victim like Umar Khalid': Tarun Tejpal seeks leniency in rape case conviction
description: The Bombay high court has recently convicted Tarun Tejpal in connection with a 2013 rape case, resulting in a ten-year term of rigorous imprisonment after his acquittal was set aside. Tejpal, alleging political victimization, appealed for leniency, while the court has provided him with a two-week window to surrender. This verdict is linked to a reported incident in a hotel elevator that occurred thirteen years prior.

title: 81 years after Hiroshima, Indian subcontinent most at risk of nuclear flashpoint
description: The article details the historical introduction of nuclear weapons and their proliferation. India and Pakistan possess comparable nuclear arsenals, with differing strategic doctrines. India maintains a No First Use policy and a credible minimum deterrent. Pakistan employs full-spectrum deterrence, offsetting conventional military inferiority. These divergent approaches shape the strategic balance and potential for conflict in South Asia.

title: Why analogue paneer is booming in India — and why states are cracking down
description: Analogue paneer, a cheaper substitute, is now facing strict government action.  Gujarat and Maharashtra have banned its sale due to adulteration concerns.  These states are prioritizing consumer protection over mere labelling violations.  The crackdown highlights the growing problem of food adulteration across India.  This move signals a significant shift in regulatory enforcement for dairy products.

title: FIFA apologises but backs Infantino after World Cup sell-off controversy
description: FIFA has recognised and apologised for the mismanagement of its World Cup commercialisation strategy. Senior officials expressed unwavering support for president Gianni Infantino despite the plan's retraction. As criticism escalates from various football entities, the European Leagues association deems the plan perilous, calling for reforms in governance.

title: Trump administration refunds $100 billion in tariffs struck down by US Supreme Court
description: In a significant move, the Trump administration has reimbursed nearly one hundred billion dollars in tariffs after the Supreme Court ruled against wide-ranging duties. By July, around sixty percent of these tariffs were refunded to importers. The court's decision emphasized that the existing law did not provide blanket authority for imposing tariffs. Moving forward, Trump is leveraging alternative legal channels to impose new tariffs.

title: From Hiroshima to dystopia: Why it’s essential to keep imagining the end of the world
'It means I've played a bit': Starc on verge of breaking Kapil Dev's Test record
description: Australian pacer Mitchell Starc is just one wicket away from equaling the legendary Kapil Dev's career tally. As he sets his sights on surpassing Dale Steyn's remarkable wicket record, Starc emphasises the importance of continuous improvement over personal achievements. This mindset has played a crucial role in his enduring success on the field.

title: Neil Armstrong's boyhood home built in 1908 hits market for $430,000
description: For sale is the childhood home of Neil Armstrong in Wapakoneta, Ohio, a historic two-storey residence that has been lovingly preserved for nearly forty years. This house boasts many original features that tie it to the first man on the Moon, making it a site of interest for history buffs and space enthusiasts alike. The current owner hopes the new buyer will continue to honor its significant legacy.

title: Tarun Tejpal to move SC after Bombay HC conviction in rape case
description: The Bombay high court convicted Tarun Tejpal of rape and outraging modesty. This verdict overturned his previous acquittal by a Goa sessions court. Tejpal stated he is a political victim and will appeal the high court's decision. Former investigating officer and Advocate General welcomed the judgment for justice. The case involved allegations from a junior colleague in 2013.

title: PD is short form for Pandits in SP's PDA, says Akhilesh Yadav
description: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav stated PDA's 'PD' signifies Pandits, expanding the party's core voter base.  He asserted Brahmins faced pain under the BJP government, citing specific incidents.  Yadav recalled the alleged torture and murder of a doctor in Sultanpur.  He also mentioned the Vikas Dubey encounter and restrictions on Swami Avimukteshwaranand.  The party leader highlighted socialist thinker Janeshwar Mishra's legacy and SP's embrace of Brahmin leaders.

title: After 'ban' on Claude Code, Microsoft has more 'bad news' for Anthropic
description: Microsoft has told engineers that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for" in a new internal memo from EVP Jay Parikh. The memo makes OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default internal model, replacing an auto-router that had been sending GitHub Copilot workloads to Anthropic's Claude. Every Microsoft division now carries an AI token budget target, months after Claude Code licences were cancelled.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
description: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.
